evidence: Ellipsometric measurements obtained a growth rate of 1.1 A/AB cycle on the Si(100) substrate at the optimal reaction conditions. Atomic force microscope images revealed that the Al2O3 films were exceptionally flat with a surface roughness of only + 3 A (rms) after the deposition of ~ 270 using 250 AB reaction cycles. Transmission FTIR studies have also been employed to monitor both half-reactions in the binary reaction sequence versus reactant exposure and substrate temperature. The infrared beam passed through a pair of 0.5 inch thick CsI windows on the central deposition chamber. The surface analysis chamber was equipped with a UTI100C mass spectrometer. The pore size of the alumina membranes was measured before and after the atomic layer controlled deposition using liquid-liquid displacement porosimetry. The H2 and N2 gas fluxes through the membranes were determined prior to the pore size measurements. The gas flux measurements were performed at 293 K. The H2/N2 separation factor was consistent with mixed molecular and viscous flow through the pores of the alumina membrane. The pore diameter measured using liquid-liquid displacement porosimetry techniques also decreased progressively from ~ 220 to ~ 130 A after 120 AB reaction cycles.
